purpose: Teach: 乗務/境遇/エキスパート/未経験/県議会/等級/書名/修得

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 乗務員のシフトを見直しましょう
lines.style: Clear, professional opening. Measured pace, decisive—she's proposing a concrete step. Straightforward delivery without overemphasis.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。様々な境遇のお客様への配慮を強化します
lines.en: Yes. We'll strengthen our attention to customers in different circumstances.
lines.style: Attentive, responsive. A slight pause before 「We'll」 to show he's already thinking through what she's suggested. Collaborative tone—he's not just accepting orders.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 外部のエキスパートと相談しましょう
lines.en: Let's consult with outside experts on this.
lines.style: Direct instruction, calm authority. Matter-of-fact pacing. Not rushing, but not lingering—she knows what needs to happen next.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。未経験スタッフ向けマニュアルを整備しました
lines.en: Yes. I've already prepared a manual for inexperienced staff.
lines.style: Slightly proud undertone—he's already thought ahead. Steady, not boasting. A small note of readiness in his voice.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 県議会の決定に注目しましょう
lines.en: We should pay close attention to the prefectural assembly's decision.
lines.style: Thoughtful, careful. She's bringing in context they might miss. Slight emphasis on 「should」—it matters. Calm but attentive.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。お得意様の会員等級を見直します
lines.en: Yes. I'll review our VIP member tier system.
lines.style: Accepting the note seriously. No rush. He's already cataloguing what needs doing. Professional, reliable.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 新雑誌の書名候補を社員投票で決めましょう
lines.en: Let's have the staff vote on the new magazine title candidates.
lines.style: Inviting, collaborative—she's including everyone. Light, inclusive tone. A small shift toward opening the decision-making outward.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。社内技術修得プログラムを継続します
lines.en: Yes. I'll keep running the technical skills acquisition program.
lines.style: Steady commitment. Quiet confidence in continuity. Closing statement—he's bringing things back to what matters. Not rushed, but final.
